questions.question: Describe how Cecil John Rhodes built the De Beers Mining Company.
questions.expected_answer: Rhodes, a vicar's son born in 1853, came to Natal in 1870 for his health, joined his brother Herbert, and in 1871 moved to the diamond fields, taking over claims in the De Beers Mine. With Charles Rudd he earned steady income from contracts to pump water from flooded mines, and used it to buy more claims. In 1880 they formed the De Beers Mining Company, a joint-stock company with capital of 200 000 pounds, raising money by selling shares to buy machinery and claims. Rhodes bought out other holders until by 1887 the company owned the whole De Beers Mine. He was helped by the financier Alfred Beit and gained Rothschild support; he entered the Cape Parliament in 1881.

questions.question: Explain how Rhodes gained control of Kimberley Central and formed De Beers Consolidated Mines.
questions.expected_answer: Falling prices from overproduction convinced both Rhodes and Barnato that controlling all the mines would control supply and price. The French Company owned key claims in the Kimberley Mine. With Beit's help and Rothschild backing, Rhodes raised money to buy it; when Barnato counter-bid, Rhodes sold the French Company to Kimberley Central for a fifth of its shares and cash. Rhodes and allies then bought more Kimberley Central shares until they held a majority. Barnato agreed to merge and became a life governor. De Beers Consolidated Mines was registered on 13 March 1888; after a legal challenge, Kimberley Central was wound up and bought by a cheque of 5 338 650 pounds in 1889. De Beers soon added Dutoitspan and Bultfontein and controlled about 90 percent of world production.

questions.question: Evaluate the significance of Rhodes's diamond wealth for southern Africa.
questions.expected_answer: The monopoly let De Beers reduce output to raise prices, close operations, lay off workers and extend closed compounds. The broad trust deed let the company acquire land, build railways and govern territory. Rhodes invested in Witwatersrand gold through Gold Fields of South Africa in 1887, obtained a charter for the British South Africa Company in 1889, which colonised Rhodesia and conquered the Ndebele in 1893 and crushed the risings of 1896 and 1897. As Cape Prime Minister from 1890 he passed the Franchise and Ballot Act of 1892, reducing black voters, and the Glen Grey Act of 1894, limiting African landholding and imposing a labour tax. He resigned after the Jameson Raid. His legacy includes the Rhodes Scholarships but also conquest, dispossession and racist policies, which is why it is debated, as in Rhodes Must Fall in 2015.
